All 15 tests pass. Every module had a bug, now fixed:

- **wrap** — used `<` instead of `<=` (lines could exceed width when a word fit exactly), and appended an empty last line for empty input. Now joins with the space accounted for, and returns `[]` for empty/whitespace-only text.
- **slug** — replaced each punctuation char with a hyphen instead of collapsing runs, and left leading/trailing hyphens. Now collapses runs and strips edges (`_a__b_` → `a-b`).
- **roman** — `to_roman` produced additive-only numerals (1994 → "MDCCCCLXXXXIIII") and accepted 0/negatives; `from_roman` ignored subtractive pairs. Now uses subtractive pairs both ways and raises `ValueError` for n < 1.
- **stats** — was case-sensitive, kept punctuation, and broke ties arbitrarily. Now lowercases, strips punctuation, and breaks ties alphabetically.
- **table** — column widths came only from row 0. Now takes the max across all rows; empty table returns `""`; trailing padding on the last column is stripped so cells stay clean.
- **dates** — the slash format parsed as day/month/year; per the docstring it's US month/day/year. Fixed, and all three formats verified (including `12/31/2026`, which would fail under d/m/y).

New tests cover all the edge cases you listed: exact-width wrapping, over-long words, empty input; slug punctuation runs/underscores/edges; subtractive roman pairs in both directions plus `ValueError` for 0 and negatives; case/punctuation-insensitive frequencies with alphabetical ties; widest cell in a non-first row and empty tables; all three date formats with US slashes.

All done — every module had a bug, all are fixed, and the suite grew from 6 to 21 passing tests.

**Bugs found and fixed:**

| Module | Bug | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `wrap.py` | Off-by-one: `< width` instead of `<= width` (a line of exactly `width` chars was split); empty input returned `[""]` | Use `len(cur) + 1 + len(w) <= width`; don't append an empty final line |
| `slug.py` | Each punctuation char became its own hyphen (`hello--world-`), no trimming of leading/trailing hyphens | Collapse runs with `[^a-z0-9]+` and `strip("-")` |
| `roman.py` | `to_roman` had no subtractive pairs (1994 → "MDCCCCLXXXXIIII") and no `ValueError` for n < 1; `from_roman` added every symbol, so `IV` → 6 | Interleave CM/CD/XC/XL/IX/IV in descending order; raise `ValueError` for n < 1; in `from_roman`, subtract a value when the next symbol is larger |
| `stats.py` | Case-sensitive counting; punctuation kept (`cat,` ≠ `cat`); ties not broken alphabetically | Tokenize with `re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", text.lower())`; sort key `(-count, word)` |
| `table.py` | Column widths taken only from row 0, so a wider cell in any other row broke alignment; empty table crashed on `rows[0]` | Widths = max over all rows; return `""` for `[]`; strip trailing padding at line ends |
| `dates.py` | Slash format parsed as day/month/year, but the docstring says US month/day/year | Changed to `%m/%d/%Y` |

**New tests** in [tests/test_textkit.py](tests/test_textkit.py) cover exactly the edge cases you listed: wrapping at exactly the width, over-long words, empty/whitespace input; slugs with repeated, leading/trailing punctuation and underscores, plus empty input; roman numerals for all six subtractive pairs in both directions, 3888, and `ValueError` for 0 and negative; case/punctuation-insensitive frequencies with alphabetical tie-breaks; widest cell in a non-first row and an empty table; all three date formats including `12/25/2026` (proving month/day order) and invalid input.

No checks are needed here: the only file created is [audit.md](file:audit.md), a documentation file — no code was changed, so there is nothing for `run_tests`/`run_lint`/`type_check` to validate. Every value in it was taken directly from the source lines I read with grep/read_file (not from memory), and the file paths and line numbers in the audit match those reads.

All 12 tests pass. Summary of what was broken and fixed:

**Bugs fixed (one per module):**
- **wrap.py** — used `<` instead of `<=` (lines could exceed width when words fit exactly), and appended an empty final line for empty input. Now joins with the space counted, and empty input returns `[]`.
- **slug.py** — replaced each punctuation char individually, producing `hello--world-`. Now collapses runs of non-alphanumerics into one hyphen and strips leading/trailing hyphens; underscores act as separators.
- **roman.py** — `to_roman` had no subtractive pairs (`1994 → MDCCCCLXXXXIIII`) and no `ValueError` for n < 1; `from_roman` just added values, so subtractive numerals like `IV` were wrong. Now uses the full 13-value table, raises `ValueError` for n < 1, and subtracts when a smaller numeral precedes a larger one.
- **stats.py** — was case-sensitive and kept punctuation (`"B"` ≠ `"b"`, `"a,"` ≠ `"a"`), and ties weren't broken alphabetically. Now strips punctuation, lowercases, and sorts by `(-count, word)`.
- **table.py** — column widths came from the first row only, so wider cells in later rows broke alignment. Widths now come from all rows; empty table returns `""`; trailing padding on the last column is stripped.
- **dates.py** — slash format was `%d/%m/%Y` (European); docstring says US. Now `%m/%d/%Y`.

**Tests:** added edge-case tests for all six modules — exact-width wrapping, over-long words, empty input; repeated/leading/trailing punctuation and underscores in slugs; subtractive pairs in both directions and `ValueError` for 0 and negative; punctuation/case-insensitive frequencies with alphabetical ties and empty input; widest cell in later rows and empty table; all three date formats plus invalid input. Result: **12 passed**.
